key_insight: MENTOR combined LLM reasoning, evidence, and local patient counts to select more negative control outcomes with higher accuracy and positive predictive value than evidence-only selection.
clinical_relevance: The system could streamline selection of institution-specific negative control outcomes used to assess systematic error in observational studies, while retaining investigator review.
method: Four LLM agents summarize drug labels, screen candidates, resolve disagreements, and adjust patient-count thresholds.
Combines Common Evidence Model evidence with institution-specific OMOP data.
Limits reasoning to disputed candidates, using less than 40% of the computation time required for reasoning in all agents.
evidence_signal: Across 349 candidates for three drug pairs at one Korean hospital with 2.9 million patients, MENTOR selected 243 outcomes versus 121 with CEM alone, achieving accuracy of 0.83 versus 0.53 against a blinded LLM judge validated by three experts on 90 candidates.
watch_item: Single-site evaluation and reliance on an LLM reference judge limit certainty; accepted outcomes still require investigator review.
paper_title: MENTOR: An Evidence-Informed Large Language Model-Based Multi-Agent System for Efficient Selection of Institution-Specific Negative Control Outcomes
